text: Describing an app is easy. Shipping it is the hard part: specs, tickets, handoffs, reviews, and deploys.
Meet Painkiller: a self-hosted platform that turns a conversation into running software, by orchestrating AI coding agents inside isolated Docker containers.
It starts with an interview. A containerized agent runs the Superpowers brainstorming skill, asking one question at a time, often as clickable choices, until the idea is crystal clear.
The result is a written spec, committed to Git. This is spec-driven development: the spec is broken down into small, atomic tasks, each with acceptance criteria and dependencies.
Every task gets its own sandboxed container, on its own feature branch. Agents work in parallel, and you can watch every step live.

Painkiller is harness-agnostic. Pick Antigravity with Gemini, or DeepSeek through dsh, Maki, or Unreal Agent. Every harness carries the same Superpowers skills: planning, test-driven development, and systematic debugging.
When an agent hits ambiguity, it doesn't guess. It asks: it commits its work, and exits with code forty-two. The analyst answers, and the agent resumes right where it stopped.
When the agent is done, the tests run in a fresh worker. Green means merge. And every token is counted against the project's budget.
Then Painkiller pushes to its built-in Gitea, and hands the branch to Coolify. Each task gets its own preview, and production is one click away.
And if a deploy fails? The build log becomes a new task, and the agent fixes it.
Painkiller. From conversation, to spec, to production.
